Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

OlinkViz 0.1.2

Data

  • probc is now fully simulated (data-raw/build_numab_probc.R). Earlier versions held the real NUMAB project-B NPX data as “Group1” plus a jittered clone of it. The new version keeps the same 22 columns, 35,328 rows and study layout, so existing examples run unchanged. It has built-in group, time and group x time effects (always present for IL6, TNF and IL8, the assay that newer Olink panels call CXCL8).

New features

  • New OlinkExperiment S4 class for representing Olink proteomics data, designed to mirror the SingleCellExperiment package (github.com/drisso/SingleCellExperiment). Rows are proteins, columns are samples; NPX/LOD/protein-count quantifications live in assays, sample and protein annotation in colData/rowData, and dimensionality reductions in reducedDims. Includes named assay accessors npx(), lod(), pcount(), the full reducedDims()/reducedDim() API, internal-slot accessors (int_colData, int_elementMetadata, int_metadata), subsetting (x[i, j]), combining (cbind/rbind), coercion to/from SummarizedExperiment, and a show method.
  • A convenience constructor for building an OlinkExperiment from raw long-format Olink data: oe_from_long(). Assay/value/sample columns are auto-detected, an optional LOD column becomes a parallel LOD assay, and remaining columns are split into rowData (protein-level, e.g. OlinkID, UniProt, Panel) vs colData (sample-level, e.g. Sex, Group). Building from a wide NPX matrix uses the base constructor directly: OlinkExperiment(assays = list(NPX = npx, LOD = lod), colData = cd, rowData = rd).
  • All plot_*() functions now accept an OlinkExperiment directly. A new as.data.frame() method converts it to the long-format data.frame used by the plots (columns Assay, SampleID, the object’s assays such as NPX/ LOD, plus all colData/rowData columns), so calls like plot_dim_reduc(oe, type = "pca", color = "Group") or plot_boxplot(oe, assay = "IL6", group = "Group") work out of the box.
  • New unified plot_dim_reduc() for plotting one or more dimensionality reductions of an OlinkExperiment, colored by a sample covariate: plot_dim_reduc(oe, type = "pca", color = "Group"). Supported types are "pca", "umap", and "tsne" (computed on the fly), or any reduction already stored in reducedDims(oe) (matched case-insensitively). Multiple types are plotted jointly as a single multi-panel figure, e.g. plot_dim_reduc(oe, type = c("pca", "umap"), color = "Group").
  • plot_pca() has been removed; use plot_dim_reduc(..., type = "pca") instead (it also accepts a long-format data.frame, as plot_pca() did).
  • plot_heatmap() now shows the sample covariates of an OlinkExperiment automatically: when annotation_cols = NULL (the default), the colData columns are drawn as annotation tracks above the samples (sample-id and constant/technical columns are excluded). Pass annotation_cols to select specific covariates.
  • plot_heatmap() gained annotation_rows to group biomarkers into sets: the protein-level rowData columns of an OlinkExperiment (e.g. the Olink Panel) are drawn as row annotation tracks automatically, or you can pass specific columns via annotation_rows.
  • plot_heatmap() gained pathway_annotation to group the biomarkers by their enriched pathways: set it to TRUE to run pathway enrichment with gprofiler2 (needs internet), or pass a precomputed protein → pathway data.frame. Each biomarker is annotated with its top enriched pathway.
  • New enrich_pathways() runs gprofiler2::gost() on a set of proteins and returns a protein → pathway mapping (returns NULL gracefully if gprofiler2 is missing, there is no internet, or nothing is significant).
  • plot_corr() no longer draws a main title, so it can never cover the color legend.
  • plot_dotplot() comparison labels now include the grouping column name, e.g. Timepoint 2 vs 1 instead of 2 vs 1 (the title and x-axis label are updated the same way).
  • plot_violin() now aligns the overlaid boxplot with the violins: both geoms share the same dodge position, so the box is drawn centered inside its violin even when groups are present (previously the boxplot could be offset to one side).
  • The single-assay comparison plots (plot_boxplot(), plot_violin(), plot_mean_profile()) gained show_p_value and show_significant options to annotate p-values for each pairwise comparison between the x-axis levels (e.g. each timepoint). By default all pairs of levels are compared; pass comparisons to restrict to specific brackets. show_p_value prints numeric p-values (e.g. p = 0.03), show_significant prints significance stars, and both together print p = 0.03 * (requires the ggpubr package).
  • With show_significant = TRUE only significant comparisons are drawn: brackets with p < p_cutoff (default 0.05) are kept, so the plot is not cluttered with non-significant bars. Set p_cutoff = NULL to draw every comparison.
  • Comparison brackets are placed at explicit y-positions stacked above the data (~10% of the y range above the top, adjustable via bracket_nudge_y, with step_increase controlling the gap between stacked bars), so the bars no longer overlap the points/violins and are never clipped.
  • New themed color palettes inspired by bird plumage, exported as ready-to-use color vectors: pal_sunbird, pal_redcap, pal_jewel, and pal_scarlet. Each provides 5 hex colors designed to work together (high-contrast warm and cool tones).
  • New olinkviz_palettes() returns all themed palettes as a named list, or a single palette by name, e.g. olinkviz_palettes("jewel").
  • plot_corr_triangle() gained a palette argument: correlations are mapped onto 5 diverging bins using any of the themed palettes (contrast-aware coefficient labels, darkened borders).
  • New plot_pathway_network(): a “Top Up-regulated Pathways” figure combining a horizontal pathway-count bar chart with a bipartite gene–pathway network (ggraph), coloured by fold change with any themed palette.
  • Journal-size figures. Every plot_*() function now sizes its text and marks from one base size, so a figure can be drawn at its final size instead of being shrunk afterwards (which leaves text too small or labels colliding). olinkviz_options(base_size = 7, axes = "l") sets it for the session (the options are olinkviz.base_size, default 11, and olinkviz.axes, "box" or "l"); theme_olinkviz() gained an axes argument and takes its base_size from the option. With a base size below the 11 pt default (“journal-size mode”) the canvas-dependent behaviour also adapts: long titles wrap, facet strips wrap, -log10 labels are plain text (a plotmath subscript is drawn at 70 percent size, which at 7 pt falls below the 5 to 6 pt minimum most journals ask for), plot_corr_triangle() fits its circles to the grid of a single 89 mm column, and plot_heatmap() leaves out sample names when there are more than 30 (at 7 pt). At the default size none of this applies, so existing figures are unchanged (11 of the 14 plot types render pixel-identically to 0.1.1). The smallest text in a plot is base_size - 1 (tick labels), so use 7 for most journals and 9 where the minimum is 8 pt. Checked at 89 mm with a rendered text-size and collision audit at 7 pt: 16 plot types pass (boxplot, violin, mean profile, spaghetti, trajectory, regression, LMER, PCA, UMAP, scree, loadings, dot plot, volcano, heatmap, correlation matrix and triangle) as do the three new ones below. plot_pathway_network() also follows the base size, but its pathway names are drawn over node circles and edges, so check it by eye; plot_network() returns an image from the STRING service and cannot be resized.
  • New save_olinkviz() writes a ggplot at an exact physical size (mm, cm or in) as PDF (Cairo, fonts embedded), PNG, SVG and/or TIFF.
  • New plot_qc(): sample QC as median NPX versus interquartile range per sample and panel, with outliers beyond sd_cutoff standard deviations flagged and labelled, Olink QC_Warning samples drawn as triangles, and an optional colour by plate or any sample-level column.
  • New plot_lod(): assay detectability, the percentage of samples above the limit of detection for every assay (ranked, per panel), with the least detectable assays labelled.
  • New plot_roc(): ROC curves of individual proteins for a two-group comparison, with AUC and DeLong 95 percent confidence interval in the legend (needs pROC). Replicates are averaged; the direction of each marker is chosen so that AUC is at least 0.5 unless direction is set.

Changes

  • plot_dotplot() now orders the proteins by effect size (it was alphabetical), the usual order for a Cleveland dot plot.
  • plot_heatmap() no longer draws the row dendrogram when there are more than 100 rows (it is a solid black block at figure size; rows are still ordered by the clustering; pass treeheight_row to draw it) and, when show_colnames is not given, hides sample names when there are more than 100 columns. Its fontsize default is now NULL (8 at the default base size).
  • plot_volcano() labels its x axis “Effect size (NPX difference, log2 scale)” when the column is an estimate/difference column instead of printing the column name, keeps its labels off the dashed threshold lines, and uses a fixed seed so the label layout is the same on every run (it used to change). It also says so (with the largest effect in the data) when no assay passes the thresholds.
  • plot_corr() text sizes (tl.cex, coef_cex) now default to NULL (0.7 at the default base size, as before).
  • Packaging: DESCRIPTION now declares methods and utils (Imports) and Rtsne (Suggests, used by plot_dim_reduc(type = "tsne")), NAMESPACE imports methods::callNextMethod, and the .paper and .paper-system folders are left out of the build. R CMD check used to stop at its dependency check because the NAMESPACE has S4 export directives but methods was not declared.

Bug fixes

  • to_wide() (and so plot_dim_reduc(), plot_scree(), plot_loadings(), plot_heatmap(), plot_corr() and plot_corr_triangle()) failed with a parse error on long-format Olink data in which a protein is measured on more than one panel and the table has a column whose name is not a syntactic R name (Olink NPX Signature Version, Plate#, …), as in the bundled probc. The replicate-averaging step built a model formula from the column names; it now averages in pivot_wider(). A protein whose replicates are all NA is NA (it used to be NaN), and data.table input is converted first so [ behaves as for a data frame.
  • plot_volcano(transform_fc = TRUE) drew the raw fold changes while applying the thresholds and labelling to the log2 values; it now draws what it classifies.
  • plot_pathway_network() failed with “factor level is duplicated” when a protein appeared in more than one row of the table (for example a protein measured on two panels, with the Panel column as the pathway source). It now uses the strongest row of each protein. It also follows the base size set with olinkviz_options() (text, nodes and edges); at the default size it is unchanged.
  • enrich_pathways() called gprofiler2::gost() without evcodes = TRUE, so the response never had an intersection column. Because of R’s partial matching on $, res$result$intersection silently resolved to intersection_size instead (a small integer), so the returned Protein column held term-hit counts rather than protein identifiers — every downstream use (including plot_heatmap(..., pathway_annotation = TRUE)) was mapping proteins to pathways using the wrong values. evcodes = TRUE is now requested by default (still overridable via ...).

OlinkViz 0.1.1

Simpler to use

  • All plot_*() functions now auto-detect column roles from common names (Assay, NPX, SampleID, Timepoint, p.value, log2FC, …), so calls like plot_volcano(results) or plot_boxplot(npx, assay = "IL6") need no column arguments. Non-standard columns can still be passed explicitly, and the functions report which columns they guessed.
  • plot_heatmap() and plot_corr() auto-detect long vs. wide input format.
  • to_wide() now keeps only sample-level metadata when pivoting (drops assay-level columns such as OlinkID, UniProt, LOD, and QC flags) and auto-detects assay_col/value_col/sample_col.
  • plot_pca()/plot_umap() recover grouping metadata (e.g. numeric time columns) that was previously lost during pivoting.
  • olinkviz_palette() no longer warns for 2-group palettes.
  • plot_heatmap() no longer fails when main = NULL (no title).

OlinkViz 0.1.0

New features

  • plot_volcano(): Publication-ready volcano plots with p-value validation, fold-change transformation, significance thresholds, and ggrepel labels for top hits.
  • plot_heatmap(): Clustered expression heatmaps accepting both long and wide format, with annotation tracks, row/column scaling, and NA imputation with warnings.
  • plot_pca(): PCA biplots with group coloring, optional confidence ellipses, and zero-variance column filtering.
  • plot_umap(): UMAP projections with group coloring, configurable n_neighbors/min_dist/metric, and reproducible seed support.
  • plot_boxplot(): Single-protein boxplots with overlaid jittered points and optional statistical annotations via ggpubr.
  • plot_dotplot(): Multi-protein Cleveland dot plots showing effect sizes with significance-encoded dot sizes and direction-colored points.
  • plot_corr(): Pairwise correlation matrices via corrplot, with configurable display methods (color, circle, ellipse, number, shade, pie).
  • plot_trajectory(): Longitudinal spaghetti plots with individual subject trajectories and group-level LOESS/LM/GAM smoothing.
  • theme_olinkviz(): Clean, publication-ready ggplot2 theme based on theme_bw().
  • olinkviz_palette(): Colorblind-friendly categorical color palette using RColorBrewer Dark2 with interpolation for larger groups.
  • validate_npx(): NPX data structure validation with configurable error/warning.
  • to_wide(): Long-to-wide format pivot with replicate averaging and duplicate sample warnings.
  • to_long(): Wide-to-long format pivot with auto-detection of assay columns and configurable exclusion list.
  • run_shiny(): Interactive Shiny dashboard launcher for exploring datasets and generating plots.

Bundled datasets

  • 11 curated Olink datasets from Long COVID, PCNSL, Myasthenia Gravis, Tuberculosis, and Down Syndrome studies.
  • Dataset documentation with format, column, and source descriptions.

Package structure

  • 11 exported functions across 9 R source files.
  • 11 bundled datasets with xz compression.
  • Clean, consistent function signatures with assay_col/value_col/sample_col conventions matching Olink NPX long-format standards.
  • Comprehensive input validation with informative warnings and errors.
